title.narrative: Energy resilience support for micro and small enterprises in Ukraine - within the programme ReACT4UA

description.narrative:
Before the war, small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) accounted for an estimated 70% of total employment. These companies have been hit hard by the war, which has led to a large drop in profitability and job losses. At the same time, companies must turn around to meet European integration. Norad has entered into an agreement with GIZ for NOK 25 million for 2024 to maintain activity and strengthen the competitiveness of SMEs in Ukraine.
GIZ has for several years run a major program aimed at small and medium-sized companies in Ukraine, the React4UA Programme (officially known as Resilience/Recovery, Accession, Competitiveness and Trade programme, in short React4UA). Norway is supporting a specific project component that aims to secure energy supplies to Ukrainian micro and small enterprises through grants and loan subsidies. The program supports SMEs in finding solutions to continue operating despite the energy situation (power outages, etc.) that meets their direct needs, be it energy generation and storage technologies, thereby enabling them to continue to operate and foster economic development.
